content: Adenomyosis is a condition characterized by the thickening of the uterus. This occurs when the endometrial tissue, which normally lines the inner cavity of the uterus, invades the outer muscular walls of the uterus. Symptoms of Adenomyosis: Women with adenomyosis may experience prolonged or heavy menstrual bleeding. Menstruation can become increasingly painful over time. Pelvic pain during sexual intercourse is another common symptom. It is important to note that many women with adenomyosis may remain asymptomatic and not experience any noticeable symptoms. Causes of Adenomyosis: The exact cause of adenomyosis remains unknown. In some cases, adenomyosis can lead to the formation of a mass or growth within the uterus, referred to as an adenomyoma. Risk Factors: Adenomyosis is most commonly observed in women over the age of 30 who have had children. Women with a history of cesarean sections or other uterine surgeries are at a higher risk of developing this condition. When to Seek Medical Attention: It is advisable to schedule an appointment with a healthcare provider if you develop symptoms suggestive of adenomyosis. Diagnosis: During a pelvic examination, a physician may detect a uterus that feels soft and slightly enlarged. The examination may also reveal the presence of a uterine mass or tenderness in the uterus. An ultrasound of the uterus can help differentiate adenomyosis from other uterine tumors. If ultrasound results are inconclusive, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can be utilized to provide more definitive diagnostic information. Treatment Options: While most women develop some degree of adenomyosis as they approach menopause, only a small percentage experience symptoms, and many do not require treatment. For those with symptoms, pain management may be necessary. Hormonal treatments, such as birth control pills or a progesterone-containing intrauterine device (IUD), can help reduce heavy menstrual bleeding. In severe cases, a hysterectomy (surgical removal of the uterus) may be required to alleviate symptoms. Prognosis: Symptoms of adenomyosis typically resolve after menopause. A hysterectomy provides complete relief from symptoms associated with adenomyosis.
